I've pulled the figures I need, so here is the answer.

**About 12.8% of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty in 2024.** This uses the Market Basket Measure (2023 base), Canada's official poverty line. It comes from the Canadian Income Survey, and 2024 is the latest year available.

- **Official poverty line (Market Basket Measure, 2023 base):** 12.8% in 2024, up from 11.9% in 2023 and 12.0% in 2022. The earlier values were 8.1% in 2021 and 4.6% in 2020, which are flagged "use with caution". Source: Statistics Canada Table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015, released 2026-04-29.
- **Relative measure (Low Income Measure, after tax):** 13.9% in 2024, up from 13.5% in 2023. Source: Table 11-10-0135-01, vector v96520326.

The two measures define low income differently, so cite whichever one you use by name. Both 2024 estimates are rated "good" quality by Statistics Canada. The low 2020–21 figures coincide with pandemic benefits.

I can give you scripts (R, Python, Stata or Julia) or an Excel workbook that fetch these series. I can also add a Canada or other provincial comparison.

Workers in Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration (NAICS 912) averaged about **$1,883 a week** in August 2026, before source deductions. That is the latest month, and the figure is preliminary. It covers all employees, including overtime, in current dollars.

| Period | Average weekly earnings | Source |
|---|---|---|
| August 2026 (monthly, not seasonally adjusted) | $1,883.03 | Table 14-10-0203-01, vector v1560358 |
| 2025 (annual) | $1,702.65 | Table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415 |
| 2024 (annual) | $1,677.47 | Table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415 |
| 2023 (annual) | $1,703.25 | Table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415 |

- **Recent trend:** the monthly figure rose from $1,844 in March 2026 to $1,883 in August 2026.
- **Method:** this is StatCan's Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours (SEPH). It reports weekly earnings, not hourly wages. The Labour Force Survey's hourly wage table (14-10-0064) only goes down to "public administration" as a whole, so it can't isolate the provincial level.
- **Coverage:** the series is "Provincial and territorial public administration". For Alberta that means the provincial government's own administration.
- **Hourly equivalent:** I did not calculate one. The hours series I'd need for that is a separate SEPH series, and I haven't checked whether it is published for this industry and province.

I can also provide reproducible code (R, Python, Stata or Julia) or an Excel workbook of these series.

In 2024, the average total income of Albertans aged 15 and over was about **$66,100** per person. That is in 2024 constant dollars and counts only people with income. It was $66,300 in 2023, also in 2024 dollars.

The median was **$48,100** in 2024, which is a better guide to a typical person because high earners pull the average up. The 2023 median was $49,300.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01 (Canadian Income Survey), released 2026-04-29. The average is vector v107680657 and the median is v107680658. Both are rated "excellent" for data quality.
- **Unit:** These are individual incomes before tax. They are not household or family incomes, which are higher.
- **What counts as income:** Total income includes employment income, investment and retirement income, and government transfers.

I can also give you the breakdown by age or gender, the Calgary and Edmonton figures, or code to reproduce this.

Alberta's median household income is about **$96,000 to $97,000** before tax. Which figure you want depends on the source:

- **Latest estimate, 2024: $96,600.** This is median total income, meaning before tax and after government transfers. It is in 2024 constant dollars.
  - Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0237-01 (Canadian Income Survey), vector v107654786, released 2026-04-29.
  - It covers "economic families and persons not in an economic family", which is StatCan's closest match to households in this table. It is not strictly the same as "households".
  - Earlier years in the same series: 2022 was $96,700 and 2023 was $98,400.
- **2021 Census: $96,000.** This is the median total income of households in 2020, in current dollars.
  - Source: Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Profile, characteristic 229, Alberta, released 2022-07-13.
  - Census values are randomly rounded.

I have not pulled after-tax income. It is available in the same table 11-10-0237-01, under the "After-tax income" concept.

I can also fetch the Calgary or Edmonton figures, or supply scripts or an Excel workbook that reproduce these numbers.

In 2024, **12.8%** of children under 18 in Alberta were in poverty. This uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM), Canada's official poverty line, on its 2023 base. StatCan rates the estimate as good quality.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01 (Canadian Income Survey), vector v1792632015, released 2026-04-29.

Recent values for the same series:

| Year | Rate |
|---|---|
| 2020 | 4.6% (use with caution) |
| 2021 | 8.1% (use with caution) |
| 2022 | 12.0% |
| 2023 | 11.9% |
| 2024 | 12.8% |

- **Measure:** the rate depends on which poverty line is used. The after-tax Low Income Measure and the Low Income Cut-offs give different figures. I only retrieved the MBM, 2023 base.
- **2020–21:** these years are low partly because pandemic benefits raised incomes, so compare with care.

I can also pull the Canada-wide rate or the other provinces for comparison. I can also give you reproducible code for this series.

Workers in Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration (NAICS 912) averaged about **$1,883 a week** in August 2026, which is roughly $98,000 a year if you multiply by 52. That is average gross weekly pay, before source deductions, for all employees including overtime. The numbers are in current dollars and come from Statistics Canada's Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours (SEPH).

| Period | Average weekly earnings | Source |
|---|---|---|
| August 2026 (latest month, not seasonally adjusted) | $1,883.03 | Table 14-10-0203-01, vector v1560358, released 2026-10-29 |
| July 2026 | $1,877.58 | same |
| June 2026 | $1,877.87 | same |
| 2025 annual average | $1,702.65 | Table 14-10-0204-01, vector v1742415, released 2026-03-26 |
| 2024 annual average | $1,677.47 | same |
| 2023 annual average | $1,703.25 | same |
| 2022 annual average | $1,666.95 | same |

- **Data quality:** Statistics Canada rates all of these as "excellent".
- **Annual vs. monthly:** The 2025 annual figure (about $88,500 a year) is lower than the 2026 monthly figures. That comparison mixes a full-year average with recent months in a series that isn't seasonally adjusted, so don't read it as a precise growth rate.
- **Revisions:** Recent monthly figures can be revised.
- **Hourly pay:** I didn't look up hourly wages or breakdowns by type of employee (salaried versus hourly), which the same tables also carry.

I can also give you scripts in R, Python, Stata or Julia, or an Excel workbook, that pull these series.

The average total income in Alberta was **$66,100 per person in 2024**, the latest year available. The median was **$48,100**.

- The average is pulled up by high earners, so the median is the better guide to a typical person's income.
- Both figures are for people aged 15 and over with income (zeros excluded), both genders combined, before tax.
- The dollars are 2024 constant dollars, so they are adjusted for inflation.
- This is individual income, not household or family income, which is higher.
- StatCan rates the data quality as excellent.
- The average was $66,000 in 2022 and $66,300 in 2023, so it has been roughly flat.

**Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01, Canadian Income Survey, released 2026-04-29.
- Average: vector v107680657.
- Median: vector v107680658.

I can also give the breakdown by age or gender, by income source, or the Calgary and Edmonton figures.

Alberta's median household income is about **$96,000** (2020 income, 2021 Census). The most recent survey figure is similar, at about **$96,600** (2024, in 2024 dollars).

- **Census, household basis:** the median total income of households was $96,000 in 2020. This is the only figure here that counts households, meaning everyone in a dwelling. Source: 2021 Census Profile, characteristic 229, "Median total income of household in 2020 ($)", Alberta, released 2022-07-13. Pandemic benefits raised 2020 incomes, and Statistics Canada randomly rounds census values.
- **Canadian Income Survey, more recent:** the median total income, before tax, was $96,600 in 2024. The 2022 and 2023 medians were $96,700 and $98,400. Source: Table 11-10-0190-01, vector v96414571, released 2026-04-29, in 2024 constant dollars. This survey has no household unit. Its figure counts each economic family, plus each person not in a family, once. So it is a close alternative to the household median, not the same measure.

I can fetch the after-tax median or Calgary and Edmonton figures if you want them.

In 2024, the latest year available, **12.8% of children under 18 in Alberta were living in poverty**. That uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM, 2023 base), Canada's official poverty line. The estimate is rated "good" quality.

Under the Low Income Measure after tax (LIM-AT), a relative measure, the 2024 rate was 13.9%.

| Year | MBM (2023 base) | LIM-AT |
|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 8.1% (use with caution) | 9.3% |
| 2022 | 12.0% | 12.2% |
| 2023 | 11.9% | 13.5% |
| 2024 | 12.8% | 13.9% |

The rate rose from 2021 to 2024 on both measures.

**Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, Low income statistics by age, gender and economic family type, released 2026-04-29. The statistic is the percentage of persons under 18 in low income. Reference period is the calendar year 2024.
- MBM (2023 base): v1792632015
- LIM-AT: v96520326

I can also supply scripts (R, Python, Stata, Julia) or an Excel workbook that fetch this series.

In 2025, workers in Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration (NAICS 912) averaged **$1,702.65 per week**. That is gross pay including overtime, for all employees, in current dollars. Multiplied by 52 weeks, it comes to roughly $88,500 a year. That annual figure is my own calculation, not a published one.

Recent annual averages:

| Year | Average weekly earnings |
|---|---|
| 2021 | $1,651.51 |
| 2022 | $1,666.95 |
| 2023 | $1,703.25 |
| 2024 | $1,677.47 |
| 2025 | $1,702.65 |

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0204-01 (Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours), vector v1742415, released 2026-03-26. The reference period is calendar-year averages for 2021 to 2025, and StatCan rates the data quality as excellent.
- **Scope:** The series covers payroll employees. It is gross pay before deductions and doesn't include the self-employed.
- **Territorial component:** The industry category is "provincial and territorial public administration". For Alberta that means the provincial government, since the category has no territorial component there.
- **No hourly wage:** StatCan's hourly wage table for this kind of breakdown (14-10-0064) only goes down to "Public administration" as a whole. It has no provincial-only hourly figure.

I can also pull the hourly-paid versus salaried split, the monthly series (Table 14-10-0203-01), or code to reproduce this.

In Alberta, the average total income per person aged 15 and over was **$66,100** in 2024. That is the latest year available. The figure is in 2024 constant dollars and covers only people with income (zeros excluded).

The median was **$48,100**. It is lower because a small number of high earners pull the average up. The median is the better guide to what a typical person receives.

| Year | Average | Median |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | $66,000 | $48,700 |
| 2023 | $66,300 | $49,300 |
| 2024 | $66,100 | $48,100 |

These are individual incomes, not household or family incomes, which are higher. StatCan rates the data quality as excellent.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0239-01 (Canadian Income Survey), released 2026-04-29. Average is vector v107680657 and median is v107680658. Both are for Alberta, 15 years and over, all genders, total income, reference year 2024.

I can also provide reproducible code (R, Python, etc.) or an Excel workbook for this data.

The median total household income in Alberta was **$96,000** for income year 2020, the reference period. The figure comes from the 2021 Census, which collected it. It is the median total income of households, before tax.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, 2021 Census Profile, characteristic 229 "Median total income of household in 2020 ($)", geography Alberta (2021A000248). The release date was 2022-07-13. I found no census table number or vector for this figure.
- **Caveat:** 2020 incomes were raised by temporary pandemic benefits, so the figure is probably higher than a typical year. Census values are also randomly rounded.

I didn't pull a more recent figure. The Canadian Income Survey (table 11-10-0190-01) is more recent, but it reports income per economic family or person living alone, not per household.

I can fetch that table or give you scripts to reproduce this figure.
